summary: Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He held a post as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-Kuei Li worked in linguistics, sinology, and tibetology. He studied at Tsinghua, Michigan (BA), Chicago (PhD under Sapir, Bloomfield, and Buck), and Harvard. He held posts at Academia Sinica, Yale, Harvard, Washington (professor of Chinese, 1949–1969), and Hawaiʻi.
Faren is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008. In 2013, he was attested as an academic advisor (教學顧問) at the University of Hong Kong.

Farzand Ali Durrani was an archaeologist and historian who studied at the University of the Punjab, University of Peshawar (~1954–1956), and University of London (~1959–1964). He served as a professor at the University of Peshawar from ~1958 to 1995.

Fawad Khan is a scholar in archaeology and Buddhist studies. He earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University, and served as Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (attested 2022).

Fazun worked in Buddhist studies and tibetology, studying under Taixu, Amdo Geshe, and Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, among others, and at Drepung Monastery. He directed the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and later became president and vice president of the Buddhist Academy of China.

Feng Youlan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Central China Normal University, Peking University, and Columbia University. He held positions at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952), the University of Pennsylvania (1946–1947), and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1946–1947).

Ferdinand Christian Baur was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tübingen and Evangelisches Stift Tübingen (~1809–1814) and later served on the faculty at the University of Tübingen from ~1826 to 1860.

Ferdinand Hitzig was a religious studies and linguistics scholar who studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1828–1829). He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen and habilitated at Marburg, where he served as associate professor (1865), full professor (1869), and Rektor (1887–1888).

Ferdinand Lessing worked in sinology, tibetology, and Buddhist studies, graduating from Humboldt University of Berlin. He held teaching posts at China Medical University, Peking University, Humboldt University, the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Ferdinand Sommer was a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate under Rudolf Thurneysen at Freiburg. He held chairs and professorships at the universities of Basel, Rostock, Jena, Bonn, and Munich (1926–1951).

Ferdinand de Saussure was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig (PhD) under Curtius, Brugmann, and Leskien, as well as in Berlin and Paris. He taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the University of Geneva.
Ferdinand von Eckstein worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer (~1810–1812) and was a member of the Société Asiatique from ~1826 to 1861.
Ferenc Ruzsa is an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1976–1982) and has served there as a faculty staff member since ~1986.
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nalanda University under doctoral supervisor Aleksandra Wenta (attested 2018).

Fernando Tola was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar educated at the National University of San Marcos. He served as a professor at the University of Buenos Aires and directed the Center of Buddhist Studies.
Filipp Fortunatov was a scholar who studied under Georg Curtius and Michel Bréal between ~1871 and 1873.

Filippo Marsili is a sinologist and historian who completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, Arcangela Santoro, and Paolo Daffinà. He held a post at Saint Louis University (attested 2019).

Finnian M. M. Gerety is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Harvard University in 2015. He completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale (2017–2018) and taught at Brown University (attested 2020).
